title: Academic Policy Handbook
content: Institutional attendance and examination policy summary.

attachments.name: Academic_Policy_Handbook.pdf
attachments.textContent:
Section 4.2 Attendance Requirements

All students enrolled in credit-bearing courses must maintain a minimum attendance of 75% in each subject to be eligible for end-semester examinations.

Students falling below 75% attendance may apply for condonation only under documented medical or official leave circumstances approved by the department head.

Repeated absences without approval may result in detention from examinations regardless of internal assessment scores.

Section 4.3 Leave Policy

Short leave up to 3 consecutive days requires prior intimation to the class coordinator.

Medical leave beyond 3 days requires a valid medical certificate submitted within 7 days of return.

title: Theory of Computation & Automata (Hopcroft)
content: Pumping lemma, regular languages, and NFA to DFA conversion textbook notes.

attachments.name: Hopcroft_TOC_Chapter_4.pdf
attachments.textContent:
Chapter 4: Properties of Regular Languages and the Pumping Lemma.

The Pumping Lemma states: If L is a regular language, then there exists a pumping length p >= 1 such that any string w in L with length |w| >= p can be decomposed as w = xyz satisfying: (1) |y| > 0, (2) |xy| <= p, and (3) for all i >= 0, the string xy^i z is in L. The primary application of the Pumping Lemma is to demonstrate that non-regular languages such as L = {0^n 1^n | n >= 0} or palindromes cannot be recognized by finite state automata.

title: Digital Logic & Computer Design (Mano)
content: Boolean algebra simplification, Karnaugh Maps (K-Maps), and universal logic gates.

attachments.name: Mano_Digital_Design_K_Maps.pdf
attachments.textContent:
Chapter 3: Gate-Level Minimization and Karnaugh Maps.

A Karnaugh map (K-map) is a pictorial method used to minimize Boolean algebraic expressions. Cells are arranged such that adjacent cells differ by only one bit according to Gray code ordering (00, 01, 11, 10). Minterms are combined into groups of sizes that are powers of two (1, 2, 4, 8, 16) to eliminate literal variables and construct the minimal Sum of Products (SOP) or Product of Sums (POS) expressions for logic synthesis.
